hypotheses.claim: A common Cognitive Law IR can compile multiple structured task families into useful synthesized dynamics rather than hand-authored solvers.
hypotheses.falsifier: No credible scaling or transfer advantage versus fixed generic dynamics or standard algorithms on any targeted family after compiler overhead.

hypotheses.claim: Verified dynamical motifs learned on prior task families reduce convergence cost on held-out structurally related instances.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reusable motifs fail to reduce median verified state updates or wall-clock on held-outs at matched accuracy.

hypotheses.claim: Mastered task families require progressively shorter trajectories because initialization and laws move closer to verified solution manifolds.
hypotheses.falsifier: Trajectory length does not decline across repeated related tasks without leakage or accuracy loss.

hypotheses.claim: Narrow verified failure regions can be compiled into repulsive structure that prunes future search without suppressing valid solutions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial counterexamples show false pruning or no meaningful search reduction.

hypotheses.claim: Second-order or momentum dynamics can improve convergence/fidelity per resource versus matched first-order relaxation on selected task classes.
hypotheses.falsifier: No matched-quality gain after accounting for integration complexity and stability.

hypotheses.claim: Repeated capabilities can migrate from frontier reasoning to trajectory/operator/law/dynamics tiers while preserving held-out correctness and reducing fresh model compute.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fresh model tokens or total compute do not fall after compilation, or held-out correctness/regression safety degrades.

hypotheses.claim: One Cognitive Law IR can preserve declared semantics across a numerical reference backend and at least one alternative physical/analog proxy backend.
hypotheses.falsifier: Backend migration changes task semantics beyond declared tolerance or full-system cost erases any advantage.

hypotheses.claim: The compiler can improve its own law-synthesis policy on held-out tasks using accumulated experiment evidence without self-certification.
hypotheses.falsifier: Improvements vanish under independent holdouts, produce benchmark gaming, or only reflect added compute.

experimentPhases.goal: Prove or kill semantic-to-dynamics compilation using ordinary CPU/GPU simulation.
Measure transfer, trajectory shortening, crystallization and failure geometry on held-outs.
Run the same Cognitive Law IR through multiple software/accelerator realizations and validate semantic portability.
Only after prior evidence, evaluate one authorized physical/analog substrate with end-to-end resource accounting.
